description:
Advances: bw.signal.query

Deliverable:
cmd/bw/signal_query.go: `bw signal query --ticket <id> [--type T] [--since <commit-hash>] [--json]` walking TreeFS.CommitsSince(cursor), filtering commits by their self-describing `signal` intent lines, reading matched blobs, returning records oldest-first plus a new cursor = current beadwork-branch HEAD. Core never persists the poll cursor — the poller owns it. md.Signals renderer in internal/md/render.go; `## SIGNALS` section in bw show (`signals` added to validShowSections for --only), trail rendered chronologically by seq (e.g. `verify PASS`, `audit BOUNCE → implementer`), including orphaned-type rendering: a stored signal whose type was removed still renders from its snapshot with a "(type not defined)" note. prompts/prime.md gains a Signals paragraph gated on the repo defining signal types (dormant repos print nothing). docs/design.md documents cursor semantics + the single-host correctness bar.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: TestSignalQueryStoreAssignedCursor, TestShowSignalsSection, TestShowSectionsListSignals, TestPrimeMentionsSignalsWhenDefined (cmd/bw); TestSignalQuerySinceCursorExactlyOnce (test/)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: bw.signal.query.poll_loop, bw.signal.query.emitter_cannot_reorder, bw.signal.query.orphaned_type_render, bw.signal.query.dormant_discovery
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: implementers run compile-graph-scoped checks only (targeted `go test ./cmd/bw/... ./internal/md/...`); no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run `make preflight`, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: verifiers run flipped stubs and targeted selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene covered: t.TempDir-isolated test repos, deterministic BW_CLOCK where timestamps render
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test (since present/absent, type filter, orphaned type, dormant repo)
- Call-site Integration: cmdSignalQuery (CommitsSince walk) and cmdShow (md.Signals) are the production callers. Proving tests: TestSignalQuerySinceCursorExactlyOnce (emit three verify signals across interleaved non-signal commits; poll --since c0 → exactly three records + new cursor; re-poll with new cursor → empty) and TestShowSignalsSection (renders in seq order and still renders a signal whose type was removed from config).

Out of Scope (files):
- internal/signal/** (validation/pipeline landed in Stages 1-2)
- internal/intent/**, internal/treefs/**, internal/repo/**
Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- cmd/bw/prime.go (added by orchestrator SCOPE_AMENDMENT 2026-07-11: the prime.md Signals-paragraph gate needs cmdPrime to supply the HasSignalTypes bool)
- cmd/bw/signal_query.go
- cmd/bw/signal_query_test.go
- cmd/bw/show.go
- cmd/bw/show_test.go
- internal/md/render.go
- internal/md/render_test.go
- internal/issue/signal*.go
- prompts/prime.md
- prompts/prime_test.go
- docs/design.md
- test/acceptance_test.go
- .spec/specs/signal_query.spec.md (verification stub flips execute:false->true only)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Single-host cursor correctness only — no cross-machine cursor work under bw sync (deferred to v2).
- No pubsub, watch mode, or consume-side hooks; no transition rules (v2 headline).
- No cursor persistence in core — recap keeps its own convenience ref, signals add none.
- No comment-restriction config; comments stay exactly as they are.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

## Mechanical checks
Files touched by ba30ae3 (11): .spec/specs/signal_query.spec.md, cmd/bw/prime.go, cmd/bw/show.go, cmd/bw/show_test.go, cmd/bw/signal_query.go, cmd/bw/signal_query_test.go, docs/design.md, internal/md/render.go, internal/md/render_test.go, prompts/prime.md, test/acceptance_test.go

- Against Allowed touches: 1 NON-MATCH — cmd/bw/prime.go (Allowed lists prompts/prime.md + prompts/prime_test.go, NOT cmd/bw/prime.go).
- Against Out of Scope (files) [internal/signal/**, internal/intent/**, internal/treefs/**, internal/repo/**]: 0 matches. No forbidden file touched.
- prompts/prime_test.go (Allowed) not touched — allowed-but-unused, fine.
- go.mod/go.sum: no changes (no new deps).

cmd/bw/prime.go assessment (orchestrator-flagged): 3-line change — adds HasSignalTypes bool to PrimeData, computes it via loadSignalConfig(store), sets it. LOAD-BEARING, not opportunistic: prompts/prime.md renders as a Go template gated on {{ if .HasSignalTypes }}; the gate cannot function unless cmdPrime computes and supplies that boolean. The gating logic must live in the prime command. The Allowed-touches list is simply incomplete — it names the template (prime.md) but omits the command that renders it (prime.go). Change is minimal and confined to the gate. Same pattern as prior stages' scope notes; flagging as a scope-list gap, not a substantive over-reach.

## Semantic checks (per must/should requirement)
1. bw.signal.query.since_cursor (must) — covered by TestSignalQuerySinceCursorExactlyOnce (test/) + TestSignalQueryStoreAssignedCursor. Would fail if: cmdSignalQuery didn't reverse-iterate CommitsSince (first.Signals[0].Seq!=1), or cursor!=RefHash(), or type filter absent (3 records not 2). Seams: none — production wiring; exactly-once drives the real bw binary, StoreAssignedCursor calls cmdSignalWithQuery and asserts env.Repo.TreeFS().RefHash().
2. bw.signal.query.exactly_once_single_host (must) — covered by TestSignalQuerySinceCursorExactlyOnce (3 records first poll, 0 second, cursor stable). Would fail if CommitsSince didn't ErrStop at `since` (duplicates on re-poll). Seams: none — production CLI end-to-end.
3. bw.signal.query.store_assigned_cursor (must) — covered by TestSignalQueryStoreAssignedCursor: emits verify with emitter-chosen timestamps 9999-12-31 / 0001-01-01, asserts Seq 1,2 in emission order regardless of payload. Also satisfies scenario emitter_cannot_reorder. Would fail if ordering used payload timestamp (order would invert). Seams: none — production wiring.
4. bw.signal.query.core_stateless_cursor (must) — negative property, covered by code inspection: signal_query.go computes cursor=RefHash() and writes no ref/file (no WriteFile/UpdateRef in the query path); re-poll test proves caller supplies cursor. Would fail if core wrote a cursor ref. Seams: none.
5. bw.signal.query.show_rendering (must) — covered by TestSignalsChronological (internal/md, deterministic: explicit Seq, proves seq-sort + orphan "(type not defined)" note) and TestShowSectionsListSignals (signals in validShowSections + showSectionNames). Would fail if renderer didn't sort by Seq or dropped the orphan note. Seams: TestSignalsChronological calls md.Signals directly (pure renderer); TestShowSignalsSection calls cmdShow -> showSignals -> store.SignalsForTicket + md.Signals (production wiring). *** DEFECT: TestShowSignalsSection is flaky — see Gaps. ***
6. bw.signal.query.discovery (should) — covered by TestUsageListsSignalGroup (help lists Signals group) + TestPrimeMentionsSignalsWhenDefined. Suppression clause explicitly asserted (dormant output must NOT contain "Signals are typed"; active must). Would fail if the prime.md gate were removed (dormant leaks paragraph). Seams: none — cmdPrime production path, real store.

Call-site integration (source-claim trace): cmdSignalQuery IS reachable — command.go registers "signal" (Run cmdSignal); signal_query.go init() rewrites commands["signal"].Run = cmdSignalWithQuery (routes args[0]=="query" -> cmdSignalQuery, else -> cmdSignal). Two init()s touch "signal" (signal.go then signal_query.go alphabetically); signal_query.go wins on Run. cmdShow invokes the renderer: cmdShow -> showSection("signals") (default true w/o --only) -> showSignals -> md.Signals. No deliverable self-contradiction.

## Intent-level scope concerns
None. Single-host only (design.md documents cross-machine deferral); no pubsub/watch/consume-hooks/transition rules; no cursor persistence in core (query writes nothing); no comment-restriction config; no dep changes.

## Targeted verification
Env: GIT_CONFIG gpgsign=false; go build ./... clean.
Flipped stubs:
- go test ./test/ -run TestSignalQuerySinceCursorExactlyOnce -> PASS (also PASS under -race -count=30, 10.7s)
- go test ./cmd/bw/ -run TestSignalQueryStoreAssignedCursor -> PASS (PASS -race -count=30)
- go test ./cmd/bw/ -run TestShowSignalsSection -> PASS in isolation, FLAKY under load (see Gaps)
- go test ./cmd/bw/ -run TestUsageListsSignalGroup -> PASS
- go test ./cmd/bw/ -run TestPrimeMentionsSignalsWhenDefined -> PASS
Extra: TestShowSectionsListSignals PASS; internal/md TestSignalsChronological PASS.

## Full-suite line
Not run (verifier tier forbids full suite).

## Audit-expanded scope
None — no prior AUDIT bounce comments on the ticket at spawn time.

## Verdict: FAIL

## Gaps
TestShowSignalsSection (a named merge-gate "Tests to pass" entry AND a flipped verification stub) is nondeterministic and fails ~25% of runs. Root cause: it emits the verify+audit signals by ranging over a Go map literal —
  for typ, payload := range map[string]map[string]any{ "verify": {...}, "audit": {...} }
whose iteration order Go randomizes. EmitSignal assigns Seq in emission order (nextSignalSeq = max+1). When the map yields "audit" first, audit gets Seq 1 and the renderer CORRECTLY sorts it before verify (Seq 2) — which trips the test's hard-coded assertion strings.Index(out,"verify PASS") > strings.Index(out,"audit BOUNCE") -> t.Fatalf("signals not in sequence order").
Reproduction (worktree, -race): 3 FAIL / 9 PASS across 12 separate `go test -race -count=1` procs; 3 failures under `go test -count=30`. The known internal/signal 1s-timeout flake is NOT involved — this failure is inside this ticket's own added test (show_test.go).
Production is correct: the md.Signals renderer sorts by Seq, proven deterministically by TestSignalsChronological (explicit Seq values). The defect is test fixture hygiene — nondeterministic emission order — which violates the epic's standing "deterministic" bounce-class check and makes the merge gate "Tests listed above pass" not reliably satisfiable.
Fix: emit the two signals in a fixed slice order (or assert ordering against the Seq actually assigned) so verify is guaranteed Seq 1 before audit Seq 2. One-line-ish fixture change in cmd/bw/show_test.go; no production change needed.

## Notes
- Spec verification stubs all executed green in isolation; only TestShowSignalsSection's determinism is at issue.
- cmd/bw/prime.go scope-list gap (above) is load-bearing wiring for the prompts/prime.md deliverable; recommend adding cmd/bw/prime.go to Allowed touches rather than reverting it.

SCOPE_AMENDMENT (orchestrator): added cmd/bw/prime.go to Allowed touches per the verifier's load-bearing assessment — the prompts/prime.md Signals paragraph is gated on the repo defining signal types, and that gate cannot function unless cmdPrime supplies the HasSignalTypes template value (3-line change, nothing opportunistic). Re-plan, not a bounce.

Separately, BOUNCE → implementer (attempts.impl now 2/cap): TestShowSignalsSection is nondeterministic — fixture emits signals by ranging a map, so seq assignment order flakes ~25% of runs against the hard-coded verify-before-audit assertion. Fix the fixture to emit in fixed slice order (cmd/bw/show_test.go). No production change needed.
